A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lateral surface correlations are controlled by the lateral confinement and by the electrostatic repulsion between the two walls, as well as by the surface charge and the surfactant adsorption.
the lateral surface correlations, as measured by x-ray diffraction and as visualized by atomic force microscopy, are a manifestation of a lateral electrostatic repulsion between similar walls.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral correlations of hydrophobic surfaces are not a simple consequence of the surface charge but are rather controlled by the confinement and the surface charge distribution.
x-ray scattering is a direct and sensitive probe to measure lateral correlations in the presence of a strong confinement, as in the SFAX geometry.
lateral correlations can be controlled by nanoconfinement, a finding of importance to the design of nanosystems.
